title: A moment you almost ignored
body: Describe one moment from today that seemed small at first, but might matter more than you think. What made it stick in your mind?

title: A belief under review
body: Pick one belief you hold about work, relationships, or yourself. Where did it come from, and does it still serve you?

title: The unfinished conversation
body: Write the conversation you wish you had. Include what you would say, what you fear hearing back, and what truth you hope emerges.

title: The first thing you reached for
body: Think about the first object you touched this morning. Describe it in detail, then write about what it says about the way you start your days.

title: A kitchen you remember
body: Walk through a kitchen from your past, real or half-remembered. What did it smell like, who was in it, and what was usually happening there?

title: What your hands know
body: Name something your hands can do without you thinking about it. Where did you learn it, and who or what taught you?

title: A stranger's small kindness
body: Recall a time someone you didn't know did something helpful, however minor. What exactly happened, and do you still think about it?

title: Ten dollars, no rules
body: You are handed a small sum of money that must be spent today on yourself. What do you buy, and what does the choice reveal?

title: The sound outside
body: Stop and listen for one full minute. Write down every sound you hear, from nearest to farthest, then say which one you had stopped noticing.

title: A skill you gave up on
body: Describe something you once tried to learn and quit. What was the moment you stopped, and would you restart it if nothing were at stake?

title: Letter from a tree
body: Write a short letter from a tree you know, or imagine, to the people who walk past it each day. What has it seen that they haven't?

title: What tired looks like on you
body: Describe how exhaustion shows up in your body, your mood and your choices. What is the smallest thing that actually helps?

title: The route you take
body: Describe a route you travel often, whether on foot, by wheel or by seat. Which part of it do you like, and which part do you wish you could skip?

title: Someone who taught you without trying
body: Pick a person who shaped you without ever meaning to. What did you pick up from watching them?

title: An argument you would like to win
body: Choose a disagreement, big or tiny, that still nags at you. Write the case for your side in three sentences, then one sentence for theirs.

title: The room you think in
body: Where do your best thoughts tend to arrive? Describe the place, the time of day and what your body is doing when ideas show up.

title: Something you keep meaning to say
body: Write down one thing you have been meaning to tell someone. Draft the first two sentences exactly as you would say them.

title: A meal that meant something
body: Describe one meal you remember for reasons beyond the food. Who was there, what was said, and what would you taste if you could taste it again?

title: If today had a color
body: Pick a color for today and defend the choice. Point to at least three moments that make it the right one.

title: The thing you carry for no reason
body: Look at something you carry or keep that has no practical use. Where did it come from, and why haven't you let it go?

title: The last time you were bored
body: Describe a stretch of real boredom, either recent or remembered. What did your mind do when nothing was asked of it?

title: Two voices in one head
body: Write a short dialogue between the part of you that wants to rest and the part that wants to get things done. Let each one make a fair point.

title: A map of your neighborhood
body: Describe the area around where you live as if guiding a visitor. Which three places would you point out that no guidebook mentions?

title: What you were afraid of at seven
body: Write about something you feared as a young child. What did you imagine it was, and what do you make of it now?

title: The person you are around no one
body: Describe how you behave when you are completely alone and unobserved. What would surprise a friend about it?

title: A rule you follow quietly
body: Name a personal rule you never announced, like how you load a dishwasher or answer messages. Where did it come from?

title: The best advice you ignored
body: Recall a piece of advice that turned out to be right after you brushed it aside. What made it hard to hear at the time?

title: Write about water
body: Choose any water you have known: a tap, a river, a puddle, a pool. Describe it so the reader can feel its temperature.

title: What you would ask your future self
body: Write three questions for yourself ten years from now. Then answer one of them the way you would if you were wise and kind.

title: A job you would do for free
body: Imagine a task or craft you would happily do without pay. What about it holds your attention, and how often do you make room for it?

title: The worst gift you gave
body: Remember a gift or gesture that missed the mark. What were you trying to say, and what did you learn about the receiver or yourself?

title: A town you have never visited
body: Invent a town you have never seen. Give it a name, a main street, a local habit and one secret that everyone knows.

title: Your earliest memory, honestly
body: Write down your earliest memory as plainly as you can, then note which parts you suspect were filled in later.

title: Something that got easier
body: Name something that once felt hard and now feels ordinary. When did you first notice the change?

title: What the clock does to you
body: Describe your relationship with time right now. Do you feel rushed, stuck, ahead or behind, and what is feeding that feeling?

title: The oldest thing you own
body: Find the oldest item you still use or keep. Tell its story, including how it reached you and what it has outlasted.

title: A compliment you could not accept
body: Think of a kind thing someone said that you brushed off. Write what you would say if you let yourself believe them.

title: Three things on the table
body: Look at the nearest flat surface. Describe three things on it and invent a short story connecting them.

title: Where your money goes without asking
body: Think of a small recurring expense you barely notice. Is it worth what it costs you, and what would you miss if it vanished?

title: A book, film or song that changed your mood
body: Pick one piece of art that shifted something in you, even briefly. What exactly did it do, and when did you need it most?

title: How you say sorry
body: Describe the way you usually apologize, and the way you most like to be apologized to. Are they the same?

title: A day you would repeat
body: Choose one ordinary day from your past you would happily live again. What would you do differently, if anything?

title: The weather inside
body: Describe your current mood as a weather report, with temperature, wind and a forecast for tomorrow.

title: A habit you are quietly proud of
body: Write about a small habit that you keep up without applause. What does keeping it say about you?

title: What you notice first in a room
body: When you walk into a new space, what catches your attention before anything else? Describe the last time it helped or distracted you.

title: The long way home
body: Imagine taking a detour on purpose today. Where would you go, what would you look for, and who might you meet?

title: A mistake worth the price
body: Describe an error that cost you something real but taught you more. Would you pay the same price again?

title: Something your family does differently
body: Write about a habit, phrase or ritual from the people who raised you that you only later learned was unusual.

title: The smell of a place
body: Pick a place and describe it using only smell. What memories does the scent bring up that sight never could?

title: If you could apologize to a past self
body: Choose an age and write a few lines to the person you were then. What do you owe them, and what do they deserve to hear?

title: A question you are tired of answering
body: Think of a question people often ask you. Write what you would answer if you were completely honest and had unlimited time.

title: The last thing that made you laugh
body: Describe the most recent time you laughed properly. What was funny, who was there, and why did it work?

title: Something small you are looking forward to
body: Name one modest thing coming up in your week that you are glad about. Write about why it matters more than it should.

title: Teach a stranger your morning
body: Explain how you start your day as if instructing someone who has never done it. Which steps would they find strange?

title: The friend you lost touch with
body: Think of someone you used to be close to who drifted away. What do you remember best about them, and what would you like to know now?

title: A fear that turned out to be small
body: Recall something you dreaded that ended up being smaller than you imagined. What did you do with all that extra worry?

title: What a chair can tell you
body: Pick a chair you have sat in often. Describe where it sits, who else uses it, and what it has overheard.

title: An opinion you changed
body: Write about something you used to believe strongly and no longer do. Who or what changed your mind, and how did it feel?

title: The loudest day of the week
body: Which day or time of your week is the noisiest or busiest, inside or out? Describe it, then describe the quiet you wish were in the middle.

title: What you would pack
body: Imagine you must leave home for a month with only one bag. List what goes in and explain the one thing you would regret leaving.

title: The thing you are avoiding
body: Name one task or conversation you have been putting off. Write down what you imagine will happen, then the smallest first step you could take.

title: A voice you could pick out anywhere
body: Think of a voice you would recognize in a crowd. Describe how it sounds and what feeling it brings with it.

title: Inventory of a pocket or bag
body: Empty your pocket or bag in your mind, or in fact. Describe each item and what it suggests about the person carrying it.

title: The thing you do better than you admit
body: Write about a strength you tend to downplay. What would change if you named it plainly?

title: A night you could not sleep
body: Recall a night when sleep would not come. What was your mind circling, and what, if anything, finally quieted it?

title: Write the label
body: Imagine a product that bottles one feeling, like relief or curiosity. Write the label, including ingredients and a warning.

title: A teacher you remember
body: Pick a teacher, coach or mentor who left a mark. Describe one specific thing they said or did that still echoes.

title: What you do with a free hour
body: If you were handed an unplanned hour right now, what would you actually do, not what you wish you would do? Write about the gap.

title: A place that feels like permission
body: Describe somewhere you feel allowed to be yourself. What about the space or the people makes that possible?

title: How you handle being wrong
body: Write about the last time you realized you were mistaken. What was your first reaction, and what was your second?

title: The view from a window
body: Look out of the nearest window and write for five minutes about what you can see. Include one detail you have never noticed before.

title: Someone you misjudged
body: Remember a person you got wrong at first. What did you assume, and what finally showed you otherwise?

title: A recipe in your head
body: Write down a dish you can make without instructions. Include the little tricks that no written recipe would know.

title: The sentence you wish you could unsay
body: Without naming names if you like, recall a thing you said and regret. What were you really feeling underneath it?

title: If your life had a soundtrack
body: Choose three songs or sounds that belong to different chapters of your life. Say what each one holds.

title: An ordinary miracle
body: Pick something you use daily that would amaze someone from two hundred years ago. Write about it as if seeing it for the first time.

title: The kind of tired that feels good
body: Describe a time you were exhausted in a satisfying way. What had you done, and how did your body feel afterward?

title: A boundary you are learning
body: Think about a limit you are trying to set with a person, a job or yourself. What makes it hard, and what would holding it look like?

title: The town you grew up near
body: Describe the place you spent your early years, or the place that felt like that. What did you know about it that visitors never would?

title: What you wish you had asked
body: Think of someone you can no longer ask, or no longer see. What is one question you wish you had put to them?

title: Narrate your next ten minutes
body: Write down in detail what you expect to do for the next ten minutes after you finish this. Then notice what you left out.

title: Something you collect
body: Whether it is objects, songs, stories or recipes, write about something you gather. What pulls you toward adding to it?

title: Pretend you are a guest
body: Imagine you are a visitor in your own home or street for the first time. What stands out as odd, charming or neglected?

title: The compliment you give too rarely
body: Think of someone you admire but rarely tell. Write the exact words you would use, and decide when you could say them.

title: A decision you keep revisiting
body: Describe a choice you made years ago that still comes back to you at odd moments. What would you tell yourself now about it?

title: The shape of your week
body: Sketch your usual week in words, with its peaks and its lulls. Which part do you feel most like yourself?

title: A creature you have met
body: Recall an encounter with an animal, wild or domestic, that stuck with you. Describe the way it looked at you.

title: What the news does to you
body: Write honestly about how you take in current events and how your body feels afterward. What would a healthier arrangement look like?

title: Invent a ritual of one
body: Create a private ritual that only you would observe. Describe what happens, what you eat, and why it matters.

title: The smallest room you have loved
body: Describe a tiny space where you felt comfortable, like a closet, a boat cabin or a corner. What made it enough?

title: A thing you are good at waiting for
body: Write about something you are patient with and something you are not. Why do they differ?

title: Dear stranger who finds this
body: Imagine someone finds this page in fifty years. Write them a note describing an ordinary day in your life so they can picture it.

title: A door you did not open
body: Think of an opportunity you let pass. Write what might have been behind the door, then what you have built in its place.

title: What you learned from a bad boss or teammate
body: Without cruelty, describe working with someone who was difficult. What did you learn about how you do not want to treat people?

title: Something you can fix
body: Pick a small thing around you that is broken or worn. Write what it would take to repair it, and whether you will.

title: A photograph you can see in your mind
body: Describe an image from your life that no camera captured. Where were you, and why did your memory keep it?

title: How you decide what to eat
body: Write about the way you choose meals on a normal day. Is it habit, budget, mood, or someone else, and are you happy with it?

title: The thing that feels like home
body: List five details that make a place feel like home to you. Are any of them portable?

title: A rumor about yourself
body: Make up a harmless rumor about you that people might believe. Then write what the true version is.

title: A time you were the new one
body: Remember being the newcomer at a school, workplace or group. What helped you settle in, and what would have helped more?

title: Slow down a minute
body: Pick a single minute from today and stretch it into a full paragraph. What happened inside it that usually goes unseen?

title: The way you talk to yourself
body: Write down a sentence you often say to yourself in your head. Would you say it to a friend, and if not, what would you say instead?

title: An object with a story
body: Choose an object in your home that has a story worth telling. Tell it to a person who has never heard it.

title: What you are curious about right now
body: Name one thing you want to understand better, however odd. What is the first question you would ask an expert?

title: The longest you waited for something
body: Describe a time you waited a long while for news, a person or an outcome. What did waiting teach you?

title: A quiet strength in someone close
body: Pick a person who is strong in a way people rarely notice. Describe it with a scene rather than an adjective.

title: Draw the floor plan
body: Describe the layout of a home you lived in as if drawing a floor plan with words. Which room holds the strongest memory?

title: What would a day without screens hold
body: Imagine a full day with no screens. Write what you would do hour by hour, and what you suspect you would feel at hour three.

title: Something you pretended to like
body: Recall a taste, hobby or opinion you faked for a while. When did you stop pretending, and what was freeing about it?

title: A tool you love
body: Write a short appreciation of a tool, from a pen to a knife to an app. What makes it feel right in your hand?

title: The thing you would ask a river
body: Imagine you could ask any river one question about everything it has passed. What would you want to know?

title: When you felt small, and then not
body: Describe a moment when you felt insignificant, then something shifted. What changed in how you saw yourself?

title: A list of things that went right
body: Write ten small things that went well recently, however trivial. Pick the one you would want to remember in a year.

title: The neighbor you know the least
body: Imagine the life of someone who lives near you whom you have never really met. Invent three details, then consider saying hello.

title: Your own definition of enough
body: Write what enough means to you in money, time or attention. Where are you already past it, and where are you short?

title: A gift you received
body: Describe a gift that felt perfectly chosen. What did it tell you about how that person saw you?

title: What the body is telling you
body: Take a slow inventory from head to feet. Where is there tension, ache, ease or hunger, and what might each be asking for?

title: A scene from a different life
body: Imagine the life you might have had if you had moved to a different city at eighteen. Describe one ordinary Tuesday there.

title: The first time you felt grown up
body: Recall the moment you first felt like an adult. What happened, and did it feel the way you expected?

title: Write a menu
body: Create a menu for a small restaurant that serves only your memories. Name three dishes and describe what each one tastes like.

title: Someone who is waiting to hear from you
body: Is there a person who might appreciate a message from you? Write what you would say, even if you never send it.

title: An honest paragraph about work
body: Describe your work, paid or unpaid, as you would to a close friend after a long day. What do you really think of it?

title: The sentence your parents or guardians repeated
body: Think of a phrase said so often by someone who raised you that you can hear its tone. What does it carry for you now?

title: A thing you would like to throw out
body: Look around for something you keep out of guilt or habit. What is it holding, and what would letting it go feel like?

title: The longest conversation of your week
body: Describe the longest talk you had recently. What did you really talk about, underneath the topic?

title: Unlikely friends
body: Invent two characters who could never be friends and put them in an elevator for ten minutes. What do they say to each other?

title: What you do when no one is watching the clock
body: Imagine a day with no deadlines. What do you work on voluntarily, and what does that tell you?

title: A risk you took that worked
body: Remember a chance you took that paid off. How did you get past the hesitation, and what would you tell someone standing there now?

title: The wall you stare at
body: Describe a wall, ceiling or view you spend lots of time looking at. What is in the details if you really look?

title: If your age were a place
body: Write about your current age as if it were a town you moved to recently. What are the neighbors like, and what surprised you?

title: The first thing you would save
body: Imagine you only had a few minutes to leave your home. What would you take, and what does that reveal?

title: A phrase from somewhere else
body: Think of a word or saying from another language or region that you love. What does it capture that your own words do not?

title: A song you cannot stand
body: Describe a song or sound you dislike, and why it irritates you. Then try, honestly, to say something good about it.

title: Dear younger me, the practical edition
body: Write a list of ten concrete, useful things you would tell a younger version of yourself. Skip the poetry and be specific.

title: Something you do for no audience
body: Name a thing you do carefully even though nobody will ever see it. Why do you bother?

title: A conversation with a stranger on a bus
body: Imagine a stranger next to you starts talking and you actually enjoy it. Write what they say and how you respond.

title: The best sleep you ever had
body: Describe the place and the circumstances of an especially good rest. What made it work, and can you recreate any of it?

title: What you are saving for later
body: Write about something you are saving for a special occasion, like a nice cup or a good shirt. Why wait?

title: A time you changed the subject
body: Recall a moment you steered a conversation away from something. What were you avoiding, and what might have happened if you hadn't?

title: A very small adventure
body: Plan an adventure that takes under an hour and costs nothing. Write where you would go and what you would look for.

title: The person who makes you braver
body: Name someone around whom you feel more courageous. What do they do, or not do, that makes this possible?

title: A letter to your phone
body: Write a letter to a device you use all day. What would you thank it for, and what would you ask it to stop doing?

title: Describing a taste to someone who has never had it
body: Choose a food, such as a lemon or a chili, and describe its taste for someone who has never had it. Avoid the words sweet, sour or hot.

title: A day you were proud of
body: Pick a day when you felt properly pleased with yourself. Describe it without comparing it to anyone else.

title: What you would do if no one judged
body: Write one thing you would do tomorrow if you knew nobody would care or comment. What holds you back from it now?

title: Your best and worst habits in the same hour
body: Notice a habit you like and one you dislike that happen close together. Do they feed each other?

title: A place you have never been but feel you know
body: Describe somewhere you have only read about or seen in photos. How do you think the real thing would differ?

title: The lesson of a long walk
body: Recall a long walk, whether chosen or forced. What did your mind do around the halfway point?

title: A thing that scares you in a good way
body: Write about something that is frightening but exciting. What would it take to move one step closer?

title: Something you could never explain to your younger self
body: Describe a part of your life now that would baffle you at fifteen. How would you try to explain it?

title: Pick a color and follow it
body: Choose one color and spend the day noticing it. Write about every place you found it and the one that surprised you.

title: The thing you say yes to too fast
body: Write about a request you tend to agree to automatically. What would a considered answer sound like?

title: When silence was comfortable
body: Recall a time you sat in silence with someone and it felt fine. What made that kind of quiet possible?

title: A story your family tells
body: Retell a story that is told again and again in your family or circle. Who tells it best, and what part has probably been embellished?

title: What your handwriting says
body: Look at a sample of your handwriting or typing habits. Write about what it might reveal and how it has changed over the years.

title: A rainy-day plan, without rain
body: Write a plan for a day where you must stay in. What would you cook, read, make or tidy, and who would you call?

title: The most useful thing you learned for free
body: Describe a skill or fact you picked up without paying for it, from a friend, a library or a video. How often do you use it?

title: Whom you would thank
body: Write a thank-you note to someone who made a real difference years ago and probably does not know it.

title: The kind of work that makes time vanish
body: Recall the last time you lost track of time while working on something. Describe what you were doing and what made it absorbing.

title: A boring object, fully described
body: Pick the dullest object nearby, such as a paper clip or a doorknob. Describe it so well that it becomes interesting.

title: How you know you are loved
body: List three ways people show you care that you notice. Is there one you wish you received more often?

title: If your worries had a shape
body: Draw your current worries in words as shapes, sizes and weights. Which one is much lighter than it looks?

title: The luck you did not earn
body: Write about something good in your life that came from circumstance rather than effort. How do you hold that knowledge?

title: A small rebellion
body: Recall a time you quietly broke a rule or expectation. Were you right, and what did it cost?

title: Two truths and a lie
body: Write three statements about yourself, two true and one false. Which one would be hardest for others to guess?

title: A city at three in the afternoon
body: Describe a city or town you know at an unremarkable hour. Who is out, what is open, and what does it sound like?

title: What you were certain about at twenty
body: Write about something you were completely sure of when you were younger. How does it look to you now?

title: The person at the next desk
body: Think of someone you work or study near. Write what you imagine they do in the evenings, then what you actually know.

title: An errand you enjoy
body: Describe a chore you secretly like, such as washing up or buying bread. What is the small pleasure inside it?

title: If your home could talk
body: Write a paragraph in the voice of your home, describing the people who live there and their odd habits.

title: A skill you would like to have by next year
body: Choose one thing you would like to be decent at twelve months from now. What would the first fifteen minutes of practice look like?

title: The first thing you check
body: Think of what you look at first on waking, whether a screen, a window or a person. Is that what you want to start with?

title: Something that happened to you once
body: Write about an event that has only happened to you once, such as a strange coincidence or an odd encounter. Tell it like a short story.

title: Open space or cozy corners
body: Do you feel more at home in wide open space, tight cozy places, or somewhere between? Describe an example and why it suits you.

title: What a good day costs
body: List what a good day for you tends to require, in time, money, people and energy. Is it cheaper than you assumed?

title: A fear you have never said aloud
body: Without sharing it with anyone, write down one quiet fear. Then write one sentence of kindness to yourself about it.

title: The stairs, the street, the lift
body: Describe the physical way you enter your home each day, from the street to the door. What small rituals happen along the way?

title: A joke that always lands
body: Write down a joke or a funny story you rely on. Why does it work, and where did you learn it?

title: The color of your childhood bedroom
body: Describe the place where you slept as a child. What was on the walls, what was under the bed, and what did the night sound like?

title: Mistakes you make on purpose
body: Think of a rule you break on purpose, like being a little late or skipping a step. What does it give you?

title: Something that surprised you this week
body: Think back across the past few days. What genuinely surprised you, large or small, and what did it show about your expectations?

title: What a stranger would learn from your fridge
body: Imagine someone looking inside your fridge or pantry. What story would they tell about your life?

title: Talk to the version of you who is stuck
body: Imagine meeting yourself at a time you felt stuck. Write what you would say, and what you would ask before saying anything.

title: Your relationship with mornings
body: Describe how you feel about mornings, honestly. Is your best self there, absent, or still loading?

title: A teacher who was wrong
body: Remember a time someone you trusted told you something that turned out to be mistaken. How did you find out?

title: The best use of an afternoon
body: Describe your ideal afternoon from start to finish with no one else's needs involved. How close could you get this week?

title: A person who tells the truth gently
body: Think of someone who can say hard things kindly. What exactly do they do, and could you practice it?

title: What your favorite place sounds like
body: Choose a place you love and write down its sounds, from the loudest to the faintest. Add one you only hear if you listen.

title: Something beautiful and cheap
body: Write about something lovely that costs almost nothing, like light on a wall or a cheap mug. Why does it matter to you?

title: Learn from a beginner
body: Watch or recall someone who is new at something. What do they do that experts have forgotten, and what can you borrow?

title: A debt you would like to settle
body: The debt can be money, a favor or a thank-you. Describe it and what it would take to feel square.

title: The first day of a new routine
body: Imagine starting a new habit tomorrow. Write the first day in detail, including the moment you will want to quit.

title: The part of a story you skipped
body: Think of a book or film you stopped partway. What made you stop, and is there any chance you would return?

title: A very short biography of a friend
body: Write a one-paragraph biography of someone you know well, focusing on a detail that most people would miss.

title: If you could redesign your day
body: Imagine you could rearrange the hours of your day however you like. What moves, what goes, and what stays?

title: Your hands at rest
body: Look at your hands right now. Describe their shape and marks, and think about what they have done in the past week.

title: A mistake you can laugh about now
body: Recall a past blunder that you can finally find funny. What changed between then and now?

title: What you would fix about your town
body: If you had one week and a small budget, what would you improve in your neighborhood? Who would you want to help?

title: The secret life of a stuffed animal or toy
body: If you had a childhood toy or comfort object, write what it was and where it is now. If not, invent one and give it a history.

title: A dream you remember
body: Describe a dream you recall, however strange. What details felt most real, and what do you think it was stitching together?

title: Who taught you to cook, or not to
body: Think about how you learned the basics of feeding yourself. Who was in the kitchen, and what did they get across?

title: An honest list of what you are good for
body: Write a quick list of what friends or colleagues come to you for. Does it match the person you think you are?

title: The unexpected comfort
body: Recall something that comforted you when you least expected it, like a stranger's voice or a certain smell. Why did it work?

title: The first day at a job or school
body: Describe a first day you remember, including the building, the people and the feeling in your stomach.

title: A letter from the future
body: Write a letter dated one year from now, addressed to you. What has happened, and what is the writer glad you decided?

title: The weight of a decision
body: Describe a decision you are facing, big or small. List what you know, what you do not, and what your gut says.

title: Something that is easier to do than to explain
body: Choose a physical skill, like tying a knot or riding a bike. Try writing instructions, then notice where words fail.

title: A neighbor's window at night
body: Imagine a lit window across the street at dusk. Invent who lives behind it and what they are about to do.

title: An award for something small
body: Create an award for an ordinary accomplishment of yours this week. Write the speech you would give when accepting it.

title: A relative you did not know well
body: Think about a family member or acquaintance you only partly knew. What facts do you have, and what do you wish you knew?

title: What you would tell a nervous friend
body: Imagine a friend is anxious about something coming up. Write the calm, practical words you would offer, then read them as if to yourself.

title: Something old made new
body: Think of an old object, habit or place you came to see differently. What changed, you or the thing?

title: The quietest hour you know
body: Describe the quietest period you can recall, whether late at night or early morning. What did you notice that is normally drowned out?

title: Your complicated feelings about a place
body: Write about somewhere you have mixed feelings for, like a hometown or an old office. Let both the fondness and the frustration have their say.

title: A thing you wish you could do in public
body: Write about something you enjoy only in private, like singing or dancing. What would it take to do it with others around?

title: The map in your pocket
body: Describe how you find your way in unfamiliar places. Are you someone who asks, studies, wanders or follows?

title: A day without comparison
body: Imagine going through a full day without measuring yourself against anyone. What would you notice, and what might you do differently?

title: The thing your body does well
body: Write about something your body does well, whether running, resting, lifting or healing. Say thank you in specific terms.

title: A fiction from a headline
body: Choose any ordinary event, like a delayed train or a lost umbrella, and turn it into a three-sentence story with a twist.

title: What you do when you are overwhelmed
body: Describe the first things that go when life gets too full. What do you drop, and what do you cling to?

title: A pair of shoes
body: Choose a pair of shoes you have owned. Where did they take you, and what shape are they in now?

title: The best question you were ever asked
body: Recall a question someone asked you that made you stop and think. Why did it land, and have you answered it yet?

title: What would your younger self think of your life
body: Write what a ten-year-old you would think about your daily life now. What would impress them, and what would bore them?

title: A bridge you built
body: Think of a relationship you repaired or created across a gap. What made the first step possible?

title: Nothing planned
body: Write about an entirely unplanned day. What would you want it to contain, and what would you be nervous about?

title: A word you overuse
body: Notice a word or phrase you say too often, such as just, sorry or literally. What does it do for you, and what is it covering?

title: The sky today
body: Look at the sky, or recall it from earlier. Describe it in detail, including a shape or color you could not name at once.

title: A small act of courage
body: Write about a quiet, unglamorous moment when you did something that was hard for you. Nobody may have noticed.

title: The things you would tell a new neighbor
body: Write a short welcome note for someone moving in near you. What are the useful secrets of the area?

title: How you celebrate
body: Describe how you mark good news. Is it loud or quiet, shared or alone, and does it feel right for you?

title: When a plan fell apart
body: Recall a plan that collapsed. What did you do in the first hour afterward, and what happened next?

title: What your shoulders are carrying
body: Notice what sits on your shoulders right now, literally or otherwise. Name each item and decide which you could set down for a day.

title: A character in your life
body: Describe a real person in your life as though they were a character in a novel, with a want, a flaw and a habit.

title: An unexpected friendship
body: Write about a friendship that formed in an odd way or with someone quite different from you. What connects you?

title: A tool you wish existed
body: Invent a gadget or service that would improve your daily life in a small way. How would it work, and what would it cost?

title: Your most trusted routine
body: Describe a routine you rely on when things get hard. Why does it work for you?

title: A time you listened well
body: Recall a moment when you listened carefully to someone. What did you notice, and what did they need that they did not say?

title: Dinner with three people
body: You can invite any three people, living or not, to a simple dinner. Who comes, what do you serve, and what do you ask first?

title: A place you found by accident
body: Describe somewhere you stumbled across by mistake that turned out to be good. What would you have missed if you had been on time?

title: Why you do what you do
body: Pick your main activity, such as a job, caregiving or study. Write down three reasons for it, from the most surface-level to the most honest.

title: The oldest friend you have
body: Write about the longest friendship in your life. What has kept it going, and what has changed between you?

title: A scar and its story
body: Describe a mark on your body or an object, and the story behind how it got there. Keep it factual, then add one feeling.

title: Something you borrowed and never returned
body: Recall something you took on loan and kept, or something someone kept from you. How does it feel to think about it now?

title: The conversation in your head on the commute
body: Write down what your mind rehearses or replays when you travel or walk. Is it useful, or is it a loop?

title: What you hope people say about you
body: Write the first three sentences you hope someone would use to describe you, five years from now. Are you living toward them?

title: A sound that makes you stop
body: Think of a sound that always pulls your attention, such as a kettle, a train or laughter. What does it connect to?

title: A pause you needed
body: Recall a time you needed to stop and did not. What would a proper pause have looked like?

title: Write about the opposite
body: Pick a belief you hold and write one honest paragraph from the opposite point of view. What is the strongest thing it has going for it?

title: A good bad day
body: Describe a day that went poorly on paper but still contained something good. What was the good thing?

title: What do you owe yourself
body: Write down three things you owe yourself, like rest, honesty or play. Which one have you been neglecting?

title: A message you almost sent
body: Recall a message you wrote and decided not to send. What did it say, and were you right to hold it back?

title: The sort of silence you like
body: Describe the quality of silence you find most restful, whether empty, shared or filled with distant noises.

title: Your favorite kind of weather, described exactly
body: Pick the weather that suits you best, and describe it with all five senses. Why does it fit you?

title: A job you would not want
body: Describe a job you could never do for long. What about it clashes with who you are?

title: A thing you are ready to forgive
body: Think of something, big or small, you might be ready to forgive in someone or in yourself. Describe what forgiving would actually look like.

title: A friend's best quality
body: Write about the quality you most admire in a friend. Describe a moment when you saw it in action.

title: How you got your name
body: Write about your name, including who chose it, what it means or does not, and how you feel about it.

title: The long middle of a project
body: Think of something you are doing that is in its slow, dull middle. What keeps you going, and what would help?

title: An hour in a library, or a bookshop
body: Imagine one free hour in a quiet place full of books. Which shelf do you head to, and what do you carry out?

title: What do you want more of
body: Write about one thing you want more of in your days, whether it is time outside, laughter or quiet. Name one small way to get it.

title: A morning from a long time ago
body: Describe a morning from many years back as clearly as you can. What was the light like, and who was nearby?

title: What you know about a stranger's day
body: Watch someone for a moment, on the street or on a screen. From their posture and pace, write the day they have probably had.

title: The thing you stopped noticing
body: Name something in your home or routine that you once loved and have stopped seeing. Look again and describe it afresh.

title: A decision made by default
body: Think of an area of your life that is the way it is because you never decided. Would you choose it now?

title: A song you first heard in someone else's car
body: Recall a piece of music you discovered through another person. Who were they, and what do you think of both now?

title: How long you can sit still
body: Sit without doing anything for three minutes, then write down every thought that visited. Which one stayed longest?

title: Describe an hour you spent well
body: Pick one hour from the last week that you used well. What were you doing, and what made it feel worth it?

title: Your relationship with being on time
body: Write about whether you tend to be early, punctual or late, and what that says about how you treat other people's time and your own.

title: A grown-up thing you still find odd
body: Think of an adult task, like paying a bill or booking an appointment, that still feels slightly unreal. Why does it seem strange?

title: The last time you changed your mind about a person
body: Recall a time your opinion of someone shifted. What happened, and how did you handle having been mistaken?

title: A letter from your home to its next occupant
body: Write a letter to whoever might live in your home after you. What should they know about the pipes, the light and the neighbors?

title: The feeling of finishing
body: Describe how it feels to complete something that took you a long time. Was the ending as good as you imagined?

title: Something no one taught you
body: Name a skill you picked up entirely on your own. How did you work it out, and how many mistakes did it take?

title: A person you only know from one place
body: Think of someone you only ever see in one setting, like a shop or a gym. What do you imagine the rest of their life is like?

title: What stays in your head from childhood TV, radio or games
body: Recall something you loved watching, hearing or playing as a child. What did it give you that you did not have elsewhere?

title: A thing about you that is hard to see
body: Write about a trait that others may see in you more clearly than you do. What might they say it is?

title: Paper or screen
body: Describe how you take notes, make lists or remember things. What system has worked, and what has quietly failed?

title: If you could master one craft
body: Choose a craft such as pottery, carpentry or cooking. Imagine ten years of practice and write about a typical Tuesday as a master.

title: A trip you were not ready for
body: Recall a time you stepped into something new before you felt prepared. What did you discover you already knew?

title: The best thing about being alone
body: Write about what solitude gives you that company cannot. When does it turn from restful to lonely, if it does?

title: A thing you have outgrown
body: Write about a taste, a friend group or a habit you have left behind. Do you miss any of it?

title: Who remembers you as a child
body: Think of someone who knew you when you were small. What might they say about the child you were?

title: Write a toast
body: Write a short toast to something unglamorous that deserves one, such as your kettle, your bed or your knees.

title: What you learned from being sick
body: Recall an illness, large or small, and what it taught you about rest, help or your own body.

title: An intersection you know well
body: Describe an intersection or junction where you have waited often. What happens there at different times, and who passes through?

title: The most generous thing you witnessed
body: Describe a time you watched someone be generous without any audience. How did it affect you?

title: A thing you do slowly on purpose
body: Name something you do carefully and unhurriedly, like making tea or folding laundry. What does the slowness give you?

title: A sentence from a book
body: Recall a line from something you read that has stayed with you. Write why it stuck and what you would add to it.

title: What your commute, walk or stroll teaches
body: Think of how your regular movement through the day shapes your thinking. What would you miss if it were removed?

title: How you ask for help
body: Write about the last time you asked someone for help. How did it feel, and how do you usually decide when to ask?

title: The garden, balcony or windowsill
body: Describe any plant or green thing you have lived near. How have you looked after it, and how has it responded?

title: A day when everything was slow
body: Recall a day that moved at an unusual pace. What did you notice that you would normally rush past?

title: A thing you made
body: Write about something you made with your hands or your mind, however small. Where is it now, and how do you feel about it?

title: Who you were with at the end of a day
body: Think about who usually closes your day with you. Describe that time together or apart as honestly as you can.

title: Something that does not belong
body: Describe an object, habit or word in your life that does not fit with the rest. Why did it end up there?

title: Write the rules
body: Invent five rules for living in your house or your head. Which one would you follow strictly, and which one is mainly a joke?

title: A road you would like to drive or walk
body: Pick a real or invented road you would like to travel. Describe the first hour of the trip in detail.

title: The unexpected lesson of a hobby
body: Think of something you do for fun that taught you more than you expected. What did it show about patience or attention?

title: A gift you would like to give
body: Write about something you would like to give someone, whether a thing, a skill or time. What would it mean to them?

title: When your plans met other people's plans
body: Recall a time your wishes clashed with someone else's. How was it resolved, and are you at ease with how it went?

title: Eavesdrop on yourself
body: Write down a short stretch of how you talk when you are tired or relaxed. What do your habits of speech reveal?

title: A shop you like to walk into
body: Describe a shop or market that always feels pleasant. What do you look at first, and what do you usually leave with?

title: Someone's laugh
body: Describe a particular person's laugh in detail. What happens to you when you hear it?

title: A thing you could not do before this year
body: Name something you can do now that you could not do twelve months ago. How did the change happen?

title: A loss you carry lightly
body: If you are comfortable, write about something you lost that you can now think about without sharpness. What do you keep from it?

title: The kind of help you do not want
body: Write about a time someone tried to help you in a way that did not fit. What did you need instead?

title: A promise you made yourself
body: Recall a promise you made to yourself, big or small. Did you keep it, and what happened either way?

title: A tiny, perfect thing
body: Describe the smallest perfect thing you have come across, such as a pebble, a note or a sentence. Why does it satisfy?

title: Describe a color to someone who cannot see it
body: Pick a color and describe it using temperature, sound, taste and feeling. See how far you can go without naming the color.

title: A habit you picked up from a friend
body: Think of something you do now because you saw someone else do it. Would you like to keep it?

title: The first time you were truly lost
body: Recall being lost, either on a map or in life. What did you do, and who or what helped you find your bearings?

title: A phrase to retire
body: Choose an expression you say, or hear, that you would happily retire. What would you say in its place?

title: Learning something late
body: Write about something you started later than most people, and what it feels like to be a beginner as an adult.

title: The best bed you have slept in
body: Describe a bed, couch or patch of ground where you slept especially well. What made it so welcome?

title: An honest weekday
body: Describe an ordinary weekday exactly as it goes, not as you would like it to go. Where is the pleasure hiding, and where is the friction?

title: Someone you would like to know better
body: Think of a person you have only met briefly. What would you ask them over a long coffee or a walk?

title: A thing that costs more than money
body: Name something you spend that is not money, like attention, energy or patience. Where does it go most easily?

title: The sound of someone you miss
body: If there is a person you miss, describe how they walk or move through a room. Write it so they could be recognized by a stranger.

title: Rewrite an old memory kindly
body: Take a memory that still stings a little and rewrite it with the benefit of what you know now. What changes, and what does not?

title: A conversation you overheard
body: Recall something you overheard that stuck with you. Imagine the rest of the conversation and the two people having it.

title: What you would build with a free weekend
body: Imagine two free days and a stack of materials. What would you build, fix or make, and where would you start?

title: The kindest thing you have said to yourself
body: Think of a time you spoke to yourself with real kindness. What were the words, and what led you to them?

title: Two sides of a coin
body: Pick something you are good at and something you are bad at that are connected. How do they come from the same trait?

title: A door in your memory
body: Choose a door from somewhere in your past and describe it. What was behind it, and who opened it?

title: What you want to remember about this season of life
body: Write a short note preserving something about your life right now that you suspect you will forget, such as a routine, a friend or a worry.

title: Your most used word in messages
body: Think about how you write to friends. Do you use short replies, long ones, emoji, silence? What does it say about you?

title: A good ending
body: Recall an ending you loved, whether a film, a job, a friendship or a meal. What made it feel complete?

title: Something you do to feel normal
body: Write about a small ritual that helps you feel like yourself again, even after a hard stretch.

title: A rooftop, a hill, a step
body: Describe somewhere high you have stood and the view from it. What did looking down or out do to your thoughts?

title: Who you were in school
body: Describe the student you were. Which version of you would you want to meet again, and which would you leave alone?

title: A person who changed your direction
body: Pick someone whose words or example sent you off in a new direction. What did they do, and did they know?

title: The thing that annoys you most
body: Write about a small annoyance that gets under your skin. What is it really about?

title: Cooking for one
body: Describe what it is like to prepare food for yourself alone. What do you make, and how do you treat the occasion?

title: If your phone were lost for a week
body: Imagine being without your phone for seven days. What would you miss, what would you not, and what might you do instead?

title: The most patient person you know
body: Describe someone who has real patience. What do they do while waiting, and what can you learn from watching them?

title: A secret talent
body: Name something you can do that few people know about. How did it start, and would you like to show anyone?

title: A reason to get up
body: Write about what gets you out of bed on a hard morning. Is it a person, a duty, a smell of coffee, or a stubborn habit?

title: Say it in six words
body: Write the story of your week in six words. Then expand that into a paragraph explaining each word.

title: A tiny joy from today
body: Find one tiny pleasure from today and describe it so well that a reader would feel it. Explain why it deserves a place on the page.

title: A stranger's job
body: Pick a job you see someone doing on the street, in a shop or on a screen. Imagine one hard thing and one good thing about doing it.

title: The first thing you would change about how you rest
body: Describe how you usually take a break. Is it actually restful, and what would make it better?

title: A time you had to wait for good news
body: Recall waiting for an answer that mattered. How did you pass the hours, and how did the news land?

title: What you would ask a grandparent
body: Whether or not you knew yours, write three questions you would ask someone from two generations ahead of you, or behind. What answers do you imagine?

title: What is on your mind right now
body: Write for five minutes without stopping about whatever is on your mind. Then circle the sentence that surprised you.

title: The most comfortable thing you own
body: Describe a piece of clothing, blanket or chair that you find deeply comfortable. How did it become yours?

title: Making peace with a mess
body: Describe a part of your life that is untidy, physically or otherwise. What is it protecting, and what would tidying cost?

title: A choice you would make differently
body: Choose a decision that you would not repeat. What did you not know then that you know now?

title: The shortest route to feeling better
body: Name the quickest thing that reliably improves your mood. Why does it work, and why do you not always do it?

title: A thing you are proud of that no one praised
body: Describe an achievement that went unnoticed by others. Why does it matter to you?

title: Write a landscape
body: Invent a landscape in detail, including terrain, light, sound and one human trace. Where would you stand to look at it?

title: How you take criticism
body: Remember the last time someone criticized you. What did your body do first, and what did your mind do later?

title: What the evening is for
body: Write about what you want from the last few hours of a day. Is it company, quiet, activity or nothing at all?

title: A character who is nothing like you
body: Invent someone whose values and habits clash with yours. Write a paragraph from inside their head without judging them.

title: Something you have been carrying too long
body: Name a worry, task or grudge you have held onto. Write what it would feel like to set it down for a day.

title: A conversation with your teenage self
body: Imagine the two of you at a table. What would you each want to ask, and who would be more surprised?

title: A first impression that stuck
body: Recall someone who made a strong first impression, good or bad. Did it hold up over time?

title: If you could be an expert overnight
body: Imagine waking up as an expert in any subject. Which would you pick, and what is the first thing you would do with that knowledge?

title: The fewest words you need
body: Choose a feeling you have right now and describe it in one sentence. Then write a second sentence that makes it more precise.

title: The thing in the back of a drawer
body: Open a drawer or box you rarely use, in your mind or in person. Describe what is at the back and what it says about who you were.

title: Someone else's good news
body: Think of a time a friend received wonderful news. Did you feel purely glad, or was something more tangled mixed in?

title: The last page
body: Imagine you are writing the last page of a book about this month. What happens in the final paragraph, and how does it end?

title: A day of only saying what you mean
body: Imagine spending a whole day speaking plainly, with no polite fibs. Which conversation would go best, and which would be hardest?

title: What you would plant
body: If you could leave something growing behind you, such as a tree, a habit or a friendship, what would it be and who might enjoy it?

title: A quiet kind of luck
body: Describe something that went right so smoothly that you almost missed it. Why do we notice trouble more than ease?

title: Close the notebook
body: Write a short, honest note to close today. What did you do, what did you leave, and what can wait until tomorrow?
